en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Training Rule on Being Displeased.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks looked at the bowls of others with a critical mind...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I will not look at the bowls of others with a critical mind.
One who has a critical mind must not look at the bowls of others.
If one, out of disrespect and with a critical mind, looks at another’s bowl, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
If, out of forgetfulness or through ignorance,
one looks [at the object] thinking, "I will give it," or "I will have it given."
Not for one who perceives it as a fault,
nor for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
